head: Not this
This
rows: Dissolving is the same as melting.
Melting needs heat and one substance. Dissolving needs a solid and a liquid mixing.

panels.title: Safety guide: the dissolving test
points: An adult supervises; no tasting anything
Warm tap water only: an adult pours anything hot
Wipe spills at once so nobody slips

keywords.def: when a solid mixes into a liquid so you cannot see it
a clear mixture made when a solid dissolves
a cloudy mixture where bits float and later settle

questions.q: Coffee granules disappear in water and the water turns clear brown. Soluble or insoluble?

questions.a: No: it makes a cloudy suspension

questions.q: Core: Test salt, sugar, sand and flour. Record what you see and sort them as soluble or insoluble.
questions.a: Salt and sugar soluble (clear); sand insoluble (sinks); flour insoluble (cloudy, settles)

questions.q: Extend: Leave the flour cup for 10 minutes. What happens? Explain.
questions.a: Flour settles to the bottom: it was a suspension, not dissolved

questions.q: Stretch: How could you show the salt is still there without tasting?
questions.a: Evaporate the water and the salt is left behind

questions.q: Sand in water sinks to the bottom. Sand is...
questions.a: B) Insoluble. It does not dissolve, so it is insoluble.

questions.q: A clear mixture made by dissolving is a...
Big question: has dissolved sugar really gone?
questions.a: No: it is in tiny pieces in the water and can be got back by evaporating.
